A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VAR attribution framework by the same authors. All 21 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable, and corresponding methods, experiments, equations and illustrations can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original localization and insertion results, network-randomization experiments, and qualitative attribution studies in the main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 reports original localization, insertion and randomization results, including additional attribution methods and transformer configurations, with further results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The cross-class spatial-softmax reweighting procedure is retained. However, v1 Section 4 uses one temperature, t=0.1, and a 0.01 margin above uniform probability; v2 Section 3.3 averages distributions over temperatures {1, 5, 100} and retains pixels exceeding uniform probability without that margin. These are limited algorithmic refinements.

E1.justification: ImageNet, Quad-ImageNet and COCO remain. v2 Tables 1 and 3 add Part-Quad-ImageNet results, but neither the text nor appendices define its data or task requirements. It is therefore unclear whether this adds distinct coverage or changes evaluation within the existing images.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated LRP comparisons for CNNs and substantially replaces the ViT comparator set with InFlow, Grad-Rollout, Bi-attn, T-attn, T-LRP and gradient saliency. v1's ViT comparisons using GBP, IG, Input×Gradient and Guided GradCAM disappear. GradCAM remains in ViT localization comparisons but disappears from the ViT insertion table.

E3.justification: v2 removes VGG16 evaluations and adds ViT-base-8 and ViT-base-32 alongside ViT-base-16. Reported localization metrics narrow from RA, IoU, precision, recall and F1 to RA, IoU and F1; insertion reporting drops SIC and retains AIC. The stated image counts, COCO filtering and localization blur remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The randomization analyses are substantially revised and extended to LRP and transformer-specific methods across three ViT configurations, while VGG16 analyses are removed. Qualitative attribution and deletion studies are also revised, and v2 Figure 3 introduces a keyboard/laptop/monitor/mouse comparison. The coffee-mug case is retained as Figure 7, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and similarity curves without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No change in uncertainty-reporting practice is documented.

E6.justification: Numerical results are extensively replaced. For ResNet50 GradCAM+VAR, v1 reports Quad-ImageNet RA 0.91 and insertion AIC 0.78; v2 reports 0.88 and 0.61. v2 also adds Part-Quad-ImageNet and new comparator/configuration results while removing SIC, separate precision/recall and VGG16 entries. These are revised results; the PDFs do not establish a controlled comparison between the two VAR procedures.

T1.justification: v1 motivates spatial softmax mainly by analogy. v2 Section 3.2 adds a mathematical argument using the softmax-gradient identity, its high-confidence cancellation, the cancellation problem with a naive local substitute, and a derivation of multiplicative attribution weighting. This substantially expands the formal reasoning, although it does not introduce a theorem.

C1.justification: v2 makes diagnosing isolated-logit attribution as a cause of nonspecific explanations a central contribution. It newly emphasizes that standard methods already encode rich class-specific information hidden by vanishing gradients. Its introduction also claims insertion improvements, whereas v1 emphasizes localization and sanity-check gains and reports mixed insertion behavior.

C2.justification: v1 extensively explains recall losses and weaker ViT insertion performance as consequences of emphasizing discriminative features. v2 removes most of that main-text qualification and emphasizes transformer benefits, while retaining the mug caveat and randomization limitations. It adds a substantive explanation relating BCE training to class-specific features and discouraged feature sharing in Section 5.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code availability statement and repository link, specifies class selection for insertion/randomization, and discloses input multiplication for transformer illustrations. It removes v1's explicit IG 50-step/blurred-baseline specification and blanket Captum-use statement. These documentation changes do not establish corresponding changes in the underlying implementations.

R1.justification: v2 removes the counterfactual/contrastive related-work discussion, including Gu et al. and Wang and Wang, and substantially expands coverage of transformer attribution and attribution benchmarking. It also adds positioning against Gairola et al.'s BCE-based explanation improvements. These change the research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The separate attribution-method overview is compressed into notation and examples, the method gains derivation subsections, and class-selection guidance moves to Appendix A. The supplementary material is reorganized into lettered appendices, including a new LLM-use disclosure.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column formatting, adds a pipeline schematic, replaces the cross-architecture illustration, and redesigns the main sanity-check figure. Tables replace paired baseline/VAR rows with VAR values and colored percentage changes, restructure insertion results into CNN/ViT subtables, and expand localization columns. Appendix plots and attribution panels are also extensively revised.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's acknowledged weakness in transformer evaluation with more relevant attribution methods and multiple patch sizes, adds mathematical reasoning, and announces code access. However, it removes implementation details and contrastive prior-work discussion, leaves Part-Quad-ImageNet undefined, and strengthens improvement claims despite remaining localization losses in Table 3. Identical ResNet50 rows also have conflicting average IoU gains: +37.33% in Table 1 versus +44.8% in Table 3. These evidential gains and reporting regressions leave the net quality change uncertain.
